items.headline: Russian missiles land in Poland
items.summary: Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone landed in Poland on Friday during a Russian attack on Ukraine. NATO called it a "grave violation" of Polish airspace, and Poland's prime minister said it was likely a provocation timed to European military exercises.

items.headline: Trump offers few results from Xi-Putin summit
items.summary: At a lengthy White House news conference on Friday, President Trump touted his meetings with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin but offered few concrete results beyond a joint statement. He defended his relationships with both leaders.

items.headline: Second judge blocks Trump's memorial arch
items.summary: A federal judge in Virginia said she will issue a preliminary injunction against the planned 250-foot arch, saying the project is unlikely to succeed in court. The order goes further than the temporary block issued by a judge in Washington, D.C.

items.headline: Iran war divides Congress as shutdown looms
items.summary: Republican Sen. Ron Johnson rejected tying government funding to an end to the Iran war. Republicans and Democrats are negotiating a funding deal to avoid a government shutdown next month.

items.headline: Senate passes bipartisan energy permitting bill
items.summary: The Senate passed a bipartisan bill to speed approvals for data centers and power plants amid rising energy costs and AI-driven demand. The measure has drawn environmental concerns.

items.headline: Trump replaces top cybersecurity official
items.summary: President Trump replaced the top U.S. cybersecurity official after a string of tech outages. Officials say the disruptions were not intentional attacks, but there is concern that attacks may come as AI grows.

items.headline: Most Republicans doubt midterms were fair, poll finds
items.summary: New polling shows fewer than half of Republicans nationwide consider this month's midterm elections free and fair. President Trump initially accepted the results.

items.headline: COP31 runs into overtime without fossil fuel pledge
items.summary: U.N. climate talks in Turkey ran past their scheduled close, with delegates deferring some decisions to next year. Activists and leaders criticized a draft deal that does not mention fossil fuels.

items.headline: Carney eyes China ties as leverage with U.S.
items.summary: Canada's deepening trade ties with China could give Prime Minister Mark Carney leverage in stalled trade talks with the U.S., experts say. Carney and Trump met at APEC, but no progress was reported beyond a commitment to keep negotiating.

items.headline: Senators back Van Hollen's bid to replace Schumer
items.summary: Sen. Chris Van Hollen says about 15 colleagues support his challenge to Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader. Bernie Sanders, Jeff Merkley and Elissa Slotkin are among those who have declared their backing publicly.

digest.overview:
President Trump used a lengthy White House news conference on Friday to tout his summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin while offering few concrete results. He also replaced the nation's top cybersecurity official after a string of technology outages that officials say were not deliberate attacks. A second federal judge, in Virginia, moved to block Trump's 250-foot memorial arch with a preliminary injunction. Congress faces a possible pre-Christmas shutdown when funding runs out after Dec. 11, as Democrats weigh limits on Iran war money and Sen. Ron Johnson rejects tying funding to ending the war. The Senate passed a bipartisan bill to speed approvals for data centers and power plants. A Missouri judge approved Bayer's settlement of up to $7.25 billion over Roundup cancer claims, and a federal jury convicted a man of starting the 2025 Palisades Fire.

Abroad, two Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone fell in southeastern Poland during a massive Russian attack on Ukraine that Zelenskyy said killed at least eight civilians; NATO chief Mark Rutte called it a "grave violation," and Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it an intentional provocation. U.N. climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, went into an extra day, with countries split over a draft deal that drops any mention of fossil fuels. Rights groups urged sanctions after the International Court of Justice ordered Myanmar to allow Rohingya returns, prosecute suspects and pay reparations. Top EU officials met British Prime Minister Andy Burnham at a rare summit to rebuild ties. Canada's Mark Carney signaled that closer trade ties with China could strengthen his hand in stalled talks with Washington.

fact.answer:
As sunlight passes through the atmosphere, the tiny gas molecules in the air scatter it in all directions. Blue light travels in shorter waves than red, so it is scattered much more, almost 10 times as efficiently, and that scattered blue reaches our eyes from every part of the sky.

Violet light is scattered even a bit more strongly than blue, so why isn't the sky violet? Sunlight contains more blue than violet, and our eyes are more sensitive to blue.

You can watch the effect change through the day. Near the horizon, extra scattering mixes the colors back together, so the sky looks paler. At sunset, light crosses more air, so even more blue is scattered away and reds and yellows come straight through.
fact.question: Why is the sky blue?
